request.text: Hey! Cozy 2BR apartment near UT Austin, only $650/month utilities included. I'm working abroad right now so I can't show it, but if you send the $500 deposit by Zelle today I'll mail you the keys. Lots of students are interested! - Greenview Property Mgmt, greenview.rentals@gmail.com

overall_badge.label: HIGH RISK
overall_badge.message: High risk detected. Do not send money, deposits, or sensitive personal information.

response.summary: A rental listing for a 2-bedroom apartment near UT Austin with an unusually low price and pressure to pay a deposit via Zelle without viewing.
action_checklist: Never send a deposit, holding fee, or rent by Zelle, e-transfer, wire, or gift cards.
Demand an in-person walkthrough or live interactive video call. If they refuse, walk away.
Ask for their full legal name and check the property address on municipal rental licensing records.
Reverse-image search all listing photos to see if they are copied from legitimate real estate sites.
Remember: in Ontario and many jurisdictions, damage deposits are illegal—only first/last month is permitted.

findings.title: Rent compared with local median
findings.summary: $650/month is 34% of the 2024 median for 2-bedroom rentals in Austin ($1,899). Rent far below the local norm is one of the most common signs of a rental scam.

evidence.source: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-year median gross rent (via Snowflake Public Data)

findings.title: Pay before you can verify
findings.quote: if you send the $500 deposit by Zelle today
findings.summary: Asking for money upfront before the apartment can be verified or viewed. Asking for a deposit or fee before you've seen the place, signed a lease, or started a job is how most rental and job scams take money.

evidence.detail: Official consumer-protection guidance describing this warning sign

data.explanation: Asking for a deposit or fee before you've seen the place, signed a lease, or started a job is how most rental and job scams take money.
data.why: Asking for money upfront before the apartment can be verified or viewed.

findings.title: Hard-to-reverse payment method
findings.quote: if you send the $500 deposit by Zelle today
findings.summary: Zelle is a hard-to-reverse payment method that offers little buyer protection. Wire transfers, gift cards, crypto, e-transfers, and instant payment apps are nearly impossible to get back once sent. Consumer-protection agencies in the US and Canada list requests to pay this way as a warning sign.

evidence.detail: Official consumer-protection guidance describing this warning sign

data.explanation: Wire transfers, gift cards, crypto, e-transfers, and instant payment apps are nearly impossible to get back once sent. Consumer-protection agencies in the US and Canada list requests to pay this way as a warning sign.
data.why: Zelle is a hard-to-reverse payment method that offers little buyer protection.

findings.title: Greenview Property Mgmt: identity check
findings.summary: It contacts you from a free personal email (gmail.com), not a company domain. Real employers and property companies usually use their own domain.

findings.title: You can't see it in person
findings.quote: I'm working abroad right now so I can't show it
findings.summary: The landlord claims they cannot show the apartment in person, preventing verification. Landlords who are abroad or can't show the unit are a common rental scam story.

evidence.detail: Official consumer-protection guidance describing this warning sign

data.explanation: Landlords who are abroad or can't show the unit are a common rental scam story.
data.why: The landlord claims they cannot show the apartment in person, preventing verification.

findings.title: Pressure to decide fast
findings.summary: Creating artificial scarcity and pressure to decide immediately. Scammers rush you so you don't have time to check. A real offer survives a day of verification.

evidence.detail: Official consumer-protection guidance describing this warning sign

data.explanation: Scammers rush you so you don't have time to check. A real offer survives a day of verification.
data.why: Creating artificial scarcity and pressure to decide immediately.
